method.interaction: Render the page, record descendant render counters, open the clear confirmation, then cancel it without changing list data.
method.historyCounter: Render calls of a mocked DesktopBookmarkButton descendant, one per mounted History article.
method.libraryCounter: Render calls of a mocked AnimeCard descendant, one per saved Library item.
method.baseline: Run the initial two fixture tests before modifying DesktopHistory.tsx or DesktopLibrary.tsx. Both assertions expected 800 extra descendant renders and passed.
method.optimized: Run the same 400-item interactions after memoizing unchanged result elements and stabilizing History action callbacks. Assertions expect zero extra descendant renders.
method.clock: Final regression fixtures freeze Date.now within a minute. A separate test explicitly advances it to verify relative-label refresh on the next render without introducing polling.

cases: All 400 History and Library entries remain mounted in their original order through unrelated confirmation state.
History Resume dispatches the current source and status updates do not rerender unchanged rows.
History progress updates, search, layout and spoiler changes refresh their affected content.
History relative labels refresh after the minute changes on a subsequent render; same-minute confirmation toggles retain the render reduction.
Library renders only its selected category and refreshes current history progress, bookmark membership, search and sort order.

baselineArtifacts.capture: Baseline counts were captured in the successful Vitest command output during this session. The tracked fixture test was then updated to assert the optimized counts and expanded with compatibility cases; no separate baseline log or ignored harness was created.

limitations: These measurements quantify repeated React descendant render work in jsdom using mocked card components; they do not measure native WebView2 frame rate, paint time, memory use or startup latency.
No browser layout engine runs in jsdom. Scroll geometry is preserved structurally by retaining the same markup and mounted DOM nodes; native visual and scrolling acceptance remains separate.
Wall-clock test duration is intentionally not treated as performance evidence because selectors, concurrency and test overhead were not controlled as a browser benchmark.
All rows remain mounted. No virtualization, offscreen CSS containment or reduction in mounted DOM size is claimed.
Explore already memoizes its poster cards; no speculative rendering change was made there.
